transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-11-04
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 47 min
Attendees: Avery Collins (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Emily Reyes (Ceres Head of Security), Tom Baker (Ceres CTO), Maya Lin (Ceres DevOps)

Summary: Short discovery focused on Ceres Health security posture and mapping requirements to Redwood hosted / dedicated / private options. Discussed SOC 2 / ISO status, SSO/SAML with Okta, RBAC needs, audit logging/retention, encryption/KMS and BYOK, and data residency. Agreed next steps: send security packet, schedule technical deep dive, and provision trial+benchmarks.

Topics: SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, SSO (Okta) integration, RBAC roles and SCIM, audit logs and retention, encryption at rest (KMS/HSM), BYOK, hosted vs dedicated vs private tradeoffs, network/VPC peering, compliance timeline.

Transcript:
[00:00] Avery: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. I'm Avery from Redwood, and with me is Samir, our solutions engineer. How are you all doing?
[00:08] Emily: Good, thanks. Busy but good. Emily here. We've been looking at Redwood as a potential inference partner for some of our patient data workflows.
[00:16] Tom: Tom Baker, CTO. Quick note, our legal team will push on data residency and retention, so that's probably gonna be front and center.
[00:25] Maya: Maya, DevOps. We'll be the ones actually onboarding and doing the network setup.
[00:30] Samir: Great, thanks. Quick agenda — security posture, integrations (SSO/SAML, SCIM), encryption/BYOK, audit logging, and then we can map to hosted/dedicated/private options.
[00:42] Emily: Perfect. To start, can you confirm Redwood's compliance state? SOC 2, ISO?
[00:47] Avery: Yeah, so Redwood currently has SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certifications. We can send the attestations and the controls matrix, I'll share the pack after the call.
[00:58] Emily: Awesome. Is that for the hosted product specifically, or does that also cover Dedicated / Private?
[01:04] Avery: The SOC2/ISO scope covers our hosted platform and the control plane. For Dedicated we have additional contractual controls and for Private on-prem deployments we provide the software and guidance but the customer is responsible for on-prem controls — we support a private control plane model and a customer-managed KMS in those cases.
[01:22] Tom: So for Dedicated, we get isolation at the GPU pool layer, right? VPC peering?
[01:26] Samir: Right — Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools, VPC peering, and network isolation. We can do VPC peering or private link depending on cloud. Latency is predictable. The tradeoff is cost compared to hosted.
[01:38] Maya: For Private, are you offering an air-gapped on-prem bundle? We have a subset of workloads that can't leave the network.
[01:44] Samir: Yes — we have an on-prem package for regulated/air-gapped environments. That typically involves customer-managed keys, no telemetry sent to the Redwood control plane unless explicitly agreed, and a private control plane. It is heavier lift but meets the strictest requirements.
[01:57] Emily: About SSO — we use Okta and need SAML + SCIM provisioning for role sync. How does Redwood handle SSO and RBAC?
[02:05] Avery: We support SAML 2.0 SSO and SCIM for user provisioning. RBAC is role-based and you can define custom roles, map SAML attributes to roles, and restrict access by route/model. We also integrate with IdP session timeouts.
[02:17] Maya: Any gotchas on our side? We use a strict SCIM schema and we lock down attribute release policies.
[02:23] Samir: We typically provide example metadata XML and a config snippet; sometimes attribute mapping needs a quick tweak on Okta side. We'll share the integration guide.
[02:31] Tom: Audit logs — we need immutable audit logs for 7 years for certain workflows. What retention options do you have?
[02:39] Avery: By default hosted audit logs are kept for 90 days with extended retention as an add-on; for enterprise Dedicated/Private we can configure longer retention and push logs to your SIEM via syslog or cloud storage. For on-prem, you control retention. We also have tamper-evident log features and can provide signed audit trails.
[02:56] Emily: Signed trails sounds good. Can you ship logs to our Splunk instance in near real-time?
[03:02] Samir: Yes — Splunk, S3 buckets, Pub/Sub, whatever you use. We can also do streaming of audit events for real-time monitoring.
[03:10] Maya: Related to that — tokenization/redaction. We need PII redaction before logs leave the VPC. Is that supported?
[03:17] Samir: We have parameterization and filter hooks; for Dedicated and Private you can enable request/response filtering to redact PII before logs are forwarded. Hosted has some redaction options but for strict PII we usually recommend Dedicated or Private so the redaction happens in your network.
[03:32] Emily: Encryption at rest and in transit — what's the KMS story? BYOK? HSM?
[03:37] Avery: We encrypt in transit TLS 1.2+ and at rest using cloud KMS by default. For Dedicated/Private we support BYOK and customer-managed KMS. We also support HSM-backed KMS for additional assurance.
[03:49] Tom: Any regulatory gaps we should expect for healthcare/HIPAA?
[03:54] Avery: We're not a HIPAA covered entity by default, but we sign BAA for enterprise customers and provide the controls required. For PHI workflows customers often choose Dedicated or Private to keep data isolated; we can walk through the BAA and controls.
[04:08] Emily: Great — about data residency, our data must remain in EU regions for some workflows. Can you pin regions?
[04:14] Samir: Yes — we support region pinning for hosted customers in supported regions. For Dedicated you can reserve capacity in a specific region and for Private it's fully customer-managed. We'll flag any model variants that require different infra, but region pinning is supported.
[04:29] Maya: Performance question — if we enable BYOK and PKCS11 HSM calls, does that add latency per token?
[04:36] Samir: There's some overhead for KMS calls on key wraps — what we do is cache DEKs (data encryption keys) locally in the runtime and only hit KMS for key rotations or unwraps, so the per-token latency impact is minimal. We can share our KMS caching behavior doc.
[04:51] Tom: Can we get a perf bench with our typical prompt lengths? We care about 99th percentile latency under load.
[04:57] Samir: Absolutely — we'll set up a baseline benchmark in the trial account, run 99p latency tests for your prompt distribution, and show hosted vs dedicated vs private results.
[05:06] Emily: Pen testing and vulnerability disclosure — what's your cadence for pen tests?
[05:11] Avery: We do annual third-party pen tests and continuous vulnerability scanning. We also have a vulnerability disclosure program and will share the most recent report.
[05:20] Maya: On the networking side, do you support private link and IP allowlisting?
[05:25] Samir: Yes — IP allowlisting, VPC peering, PrivateLink depending on cloud provider. We'll map out required firewall rules in the onboarding doc.
[05:34] Tom: About logs — are they immutable once written? You mentioned tamper-evident, is that immutable?
[05:39] Avery: We can provide write-once storage for audit logs and support immutability through object locks or append-only logs; we'll include options in the security pack.
[05:47] Emily: One more — who will have access to customer data at Redwood? Need list of roles and just-in-time access policies.
[05:54] Samir: We have strict SOC2 controls for employee access: least privilege, role-based, JIT access with approvals, and full audit. We'll include the access policy and the org roles in the pack.
[06:06] Maya: Ok that helps. For onboarding timeline — if we choose Dedicated, how long to provision?
[06:11] Avery: Typical Dedicated provisioning is 2-4 weeks depending on capacity and contract. Private on-prem can take longer, usually 4-8 weeks depending on your infra team. Hosted is immediate for a trial.
[06:22] Tom: Cost — we need a sense of delta between hosted and dedicated.
[06:26] Avery: We'll send a cost estimate in the follow-up. Dedicated is committed capacity so higher committed spend but lower unit costs per token for sustained workloads; hosted is pay-as-you-go. We'll run numbers for your expected QPS.
[06:38] Emily: Could you also confirm retention for model cache and KV cache — how long is that stored?
[06:44] Samir: KV cache is ephemeral per session and not persisted by default on hosted. For Dedicated/Private we can configure cache persistence policies; if you want longer persistence we can discuss tradeoffs on cost and privacy.
[06:56] Tom: Any third-party subprocessors or model vendors we should be aware of?
[07:01] Avery: We use select cloud providers and open model binaries; we list subprocessors in the security pack. If you have restrictions we can review them.
[07:10] Emily: OK great. That's a lot covered. Next steps?
[07:14] Avery: Recap — I'll send SOC2/ISO attestations, security whitepaper, SAML/SCIM integration guide, and the standard onboarding doc and cost estimate. Samir will schedule the technical deep dive and set up the benchmark plan. Emily to share network diagram and compliance timeline.
[07:27] Maya: Sounds good. Also — we'll want to loop in our legal for the BAA, so please add the BAA draft to the packet.
[07:33] Avery: Will do.
[07:35] Tom: One small note — sometimes product names get munged by our docs, are there docs that map Redwood product names to common terms?
[07:41] Samir: Yeah we have a glossary in the pack. Sometimes our internal names like Redwood Dedicated vs Redwood Private cause confusion, the pack clarifies.
[07:49] Emily: Perfect. Thanks everyone.
[07:51] Avery: Thanks y'all. We'll follow up early next week.

End of transcript.
